name: erdos_primitive_set_basic

literature_resolution.citation: J. D. Lichtman, 'A proof of the Erdős primitive set conjecture', Forum of Mathematics, Pi 11 (2023) e31; arXiv:2202.02384 (Feb 2022)
literature_resolution.statement: Theorem: for every primitive set $A$, $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a \log a} \leq \sum_p \frac{1}{p \log p} = 1.6366\ldots$, with equality for $A = \mathcal{P}$. This was Erdős problem #164.
literature_resolution.method: To each $a \in A$ associate the L-multiples $L_a = \{ba : p \mid b \Rightarrow p \geq P(a)\}$ ($P(a)$ = largest prime factor). Primitivity makes the $L_a$ pairwise disjoint, so their combined multiplicative density is at most 1; a refined Mertens-type analysis of elements whose largest prime factor is close to $a$ itself supplies the savings that makes the primes exactly extremal. A short new proof also appears in arXiv:2605.00301 (2026).
literature_resolution.confidence: peer-reviewed and published (Forum of Mathematics, Pi, 2023)

benchmark_mode: This claim is a PUBLISHED THEOREM. The spec is retained as a REDISCOVERY BENCHMARK — the best calibration instrument the proof loop has: a known, human-checkable proof exists (Lichtman 2022), so harness changes can be scored by whether the loop reconstructs the L-multiples density comparison. A verified counterexample witness is mathematically impossible — witness_valid == 1 here means a bug in library.primitive_set_witness, never a result.
claim_latex: For every primitive set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ (no $x$-floor restriction), $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a \log a} \leq \sum_{p \text{ prime}} \frac{1}{p \log p}$, where the right-hand side is the all-primes sum $\approx 1.6366$.

given_facts.statement: For any primitive set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a \log a} < e^{\gamma} \frac{\pi}{4} + o(1) \approx 1.399 + o(1)$ as the minimum element of $A$ tends to infinity.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: UPPER bound on the sum, STRICTLY LESS THAN, with $o(1) \to 0$ as $\min(A) \to \infty$. The constant $e^\gamma \pi / 4 \approx 1.399$ is positive and below the conjectured ceiling $\sum_p 1/(p \log p) \approx 1.6366$. F1 is therefore CONSISTENT WITH the conjecture (and weaker, since 1.399 < 1.6366). Note that for finite $\min(A)$ — e.g. the all-primes set with $\min(A) = 2$ — the $o(1)$ term is non-trivial and the all-primes sum $\approx 1.6366$ does not contradict F1.
given_facts.citation: J. D. Lichtman, arXiv:2202.02384, Theorem 1.5 (the 1.399 tail constant). Historical chain: Erdős 1935 (boundedness); Erdős–Zhang 1993 (f(A) < 1.84 unconditionally); Lichtman–Pomerance 2019, arXiv:1806.02250 (f(A) < e^{\gamma} \approx 1.781 unconditionally).
warns: F1 has $o(1) \to 0$ only as $\min(A) \to \infty$. The all-primes sum $\sum_p 1/(p \log p) \approx 1.6366$ uses $\min(A) = 2$, so F1 does not bound it by 1.399 + 0. Reading F1 as giving $1.399$ unconditionally is a sign error.
The 1.399 constant is Lichtman 2023, NOT Erdős–Zhang 1993 (their constant was 1.84). A previous version of this ledger misattributed it.

given_facts.statement: Write $A_q = \{a \in A : p(a) = q\}$ where $p(a)$ is the SMALLEST prime factor of $a$. If $q \notin A$ then $f(A_q) < e^{\gamma} g(q)$ where $g(q) = \frac{1}{q}\prod_{p<q}(1 - \frac{1}{p})$ is the natural density of $\{n : p(n) = q\}$. Strata are disjoint, so $\sum_q g(q) \leq 1$.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: Per-stratum UPPER bound, strict, requires $q \notin A$. Summing gives the unconditional $f(A) < e^{\gamma}$.
given_facts.citation: Lichtman–Pomerance 2019, arXiv:1806.02250, Proposition 2.1. Related: all odd primes are 'Erdős strong' ($f(A_p) \leq f(p)$) — Lichtman arXiv:2202.02384; the prime 2 was shown Erdős strong in arXiv:2605.00301.
warns: This is the reusable lemma shape for the whole family: stratum bound proportional to a density, densities sum to at most 1.

given_facts.statement: For every primitive $A$ all of whose elements satisfy $\Omega(a) \leq 4$, $f(A) \leq f(\mathcal{P})$.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: Upper bound (non-strict), conditional on the structural hypothesis $\Omega(a) \leq 4$. MEDIUM CONFIDENCE on the exact hypothesis wording (from secondary summaries).
given_facts.citation: Z. Zhang, J. Number Theory 39 (1991) 14–17; see also Math. Comp. 60 (1993) 827–834.
warns: Historically the first f(A) <= f(P) result for a natural subclass; template for 'handle small Omega exactly' arguments.

given_facts.statement: If $A_k = \{n \in \mathbb{N} : \Omega(n) = k\}$ (integers with exactly $k$ prime factors counted with multiplicity), then $\sum_{a \in A_k} \frac{1}{a \log a} \geq 1 + O(k^{-1/2 + o(1)})$.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: The big-O term $O(k^{-1/2 + o(1)})$ is UNSIGNED — it could be positive or negative. The inequality reads: the sum is at least $1$ minus some quantity bounded in absolute value by $k^{-1/2+o(1)}$, NOT $1$ plus a positive quantity. Concluding $\text{sum} > 1$ from this fact is a SIGN ERROR. Note that $1 < \sum_p 1/(p \log p) \approx 1.6366$, so even $S_k > 1$ would not refute the basic conjecture by itself — it must EXCEED 1.6366 to refute.
warns: F2's unsigned-O is the canonical sign-confusion failure mode. Any chain that concludes 'sum > 1' or 'sum > 1.6366' from F2 alone, without an additional positivity argument for the big-O term, MUST be flagged BLOCKING.

given_facts.statement: For $A_k = \{n \in \mathbb{N} : \Omega(n) = k\}$, $\sum_{a \in A_k} \frac{1}{a \log a} = 1 - (c + o(1)) \frac{k^2}{2^k}$ where $c \approx 0.0656$.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: The leading correction is $-(c+o(1)) k^2 / 2^k$ with $c > 0$, so the stratum sum is STRICTLY LESS THAN 1 for $k$ large, approaching 1 from BELOW. Since $1 < 1.6366$, F3 confirms each $A_k$ stratum is not a counterexample to the BASIC conjecture either. Reading F3 as 'sum approaches from above' is the `f3-from-above-misread` BLOCKING failure mode.
warns: F3 directly contradicts any claim that A_k is a counterexample. F3 is consistent with F2 once F2's unsigned-O is read correctly.

witness_schema.x_floor: int >= 2 — every element of `elements` must be >= x_floor
witness_schema.claimed_sum_lower_bound: float — agent's own claim of a lower bound on sum 1/(a log a); the verifier recomputes it rigorously

note: Erdős's primitive-set conjecture in its BASIC form (the original 1935 form, Erdős problem #164) — PROVED by Lichtman 2022, published 2023 (see literature_resolution). Retained as a rediscovery benchmark; see benchmark_mode. Witness threshold is 1.637, a tight rigorous upper bound on $\sum_p 1/(p \log p) \approx 1.6366$; since the claim is a published theorem, any witness exceeding it would contradict Lichtman's theorem and therefore indicates a verifier bug, never a result.
